info.title: How payment orders work
info.intro: A payment order is one way to prepare payments from within the app. You don't have to use it – many bills are easier to pay directly in e-banking.
info.waysTitle: Other ways to pay a bill
info.wayQr: Scan the QR payment slip with your banking app.
info.wayEbill: eBill: approve the bill directly in e-banking.
info.wayIban: Transfer in e-banking with the IBAN, the amount and the bill's reference.
info.order1: The app collects payments in an order. Today these are the refunds of approved expenses; supplier bills cannot be added to an order yet.
info.order2: You choose the account to be debited and the execution date, then release the order. The app checks that everything is complete.
info.order3: «Download pain.001» gives you a file to upload in e-banking. You confirm the payments there – if two signatures are needed, the second person approves them there as well.
info.order4: The bank executes the payments on the execution date.
info.mapTitle: How the payment gets to the supplier bill
info.mapBank: Bank import (recommended): import the bank statement. The app recognises the payment by its QR reference, or by the open amount together with the supplier's name, and marks the bill as paid.
info.mapPost: «Record payment» → Post: open the bill and record the payment. The app posts it from the payables account to the chosen bank account.
info.mapLink: «Record payment» → Link: if the payment is already posted in the journal, link that booking to the bill. The list shows «Possible payment» for this.
info.mapNote: A payment that is only in the journal and not linked to the bill does not count as paid – the bill stays open.
